seo_title: The Power of Matterport: 3D Scans & Virtual Tours Guide
meta_description: What is a Matterport scan and what is it used for? How 3D virtual tours work, how accurate they are, and how they help claims.
h1: The Power of Matterport: The Ultimate Guide to 3D Virtual Tours
excerpt: What is a Matterport scan and what is it used for? This guide covers how Matterport 3D virtual tours work, their accuracy, costs, CAD exports and their value in insurance claims.
key_takeaways: A Matterport scan turns a real space into a measurable, shareable 3D digital twin.
It is used in real estate, construction, facilities management and insurance claims.
Professional cameras give better depth accuracy than smartphone captures.
Scanning before mitigation preserves damage evidence that photos alone can miss.
Exports can feed CAD and BIM software for repair planning.
body_html:
A Matterport scan is a 3D digital capture of a real space made with a Matterport camera or compatible device. The software stitches dozens of scans into an interactive 3D virtual tour, a "dollhouse" model and measurable floor plans. Matterport is used in real estate, construction, facilities management and insurance claims to document spaces accurately and share them remotely.

What is a Matterport scan?

A Matterport scan starts with a camera placed on a tripod in a room. At each position, the camera captures panoramic images along with depth data. The operator moves the camera every few feet through the property, and Matterport's cloud software aligns all those scan points into one connected 3D model called a digital twin.

When processing finishes, anyone with the link can "walk" through the space in a web browser, rotate a full dollhouse view, switch to a top-down floor plan and take point-to-point measurements. No special software is needed to view a Matterport tour.

What a Matterport scan produces

  • Interactive 3D tour: a walk-through view you can explore from any angle
  • Dollhouse view: a cutaway 3D model of the whole structure
  • Floor plan view: a top-down layout, with schematic floor plans available as an add-on
  • Measurements: point-to-point dimensions taken right inside the model
  • Tags and notes: labels, photos and comments pinned to exact locations
  • High-resolution still images pulled from any viewpoint
  • Downloadable data such as point clouds and 3D mesh files, depending on plan and add-ons

How does Matterport work?

Matterport combines capture hardware with cloud processing. The workflow is simple enough that a trained operator can scan a typical home in a couple of hours.

  1. Capture: The operator sets up the camera and takes a scan, then moves it a few feet and repeats, room by room.
  2. Alignment: The Matterport Capture app aligns each new scan to the previous ones in real time, so gaps are spotted on site.
  3. Upload: The scans are uploaded to Matterport's cloud.
  4. Processing: Software builds the 3D mesh, textures, dollhouse and floor plan views.
  5. Sharing: The finished model is shared by link, embedded in a website or exported for other software.

Which cameras can create a Matterport scan?

Capture deviceBest forTrade-offs
Matterport Pro-series camerasProfessional documentation, large spaces, measurement-focused workHigher equipment cost
Compatible 360-degree camerasQuick tours, smaller spacesLess depth precision than Pro-series cameras
Smartphones with the Capture appSimple, low-cost toursLower accuracy; not ideal for detailed documentation

For insurance documentation, a professional-grade camera is usually the better choice because depth accuracy and image quality matter when the model becomes evidence.

What is Matterport used for?

Matterport started as a real estate marketing tool and grew into a documentation platform used across many industries.

  • Real estate: virtual open houses that let buyers tour a listing remotely
  • Construction: as-built records, progress documentation and pre-construction site conditions
  • Architecture and design: accurate existing-conditions models for renovation planning
  • Facilities management: digital records of buildings, equipment and utility locations
  • Hospitality and venues: virtual tours for hotels, event spaces and restaurants
  • Insurance and restoration: documenting property damage, contents and repair scope

For a shorter overview of the platform itself, see our article what is Matterport.

How Matterport helps with insurance claims

Property claims rise and fall on documentation. Photos capture moments, but they rarely show how rooms connect, how far water traveled or exactly how much material needs to be replaced. A Matterport scan preserves the whole scene in context.

Why a 3D scan is stronger evidence than photos alone

  • Complete context: every room, wall and ceiling is captured, not just the areas someone chose to photograph.
  • Measurements: dimensions can be checked against the carrier's estimate for drywall, flooring, paint and trim quantities.
  • Preservation: the damage is recorded before mitigation, demolition or repairs change the scene.
  • Remote access: adjusters, appraisers, umpires and engineers can review the property without another site visit.
  • Annotations: tags point reviewers to specific damage such as stains, cracks and burned framing.

This is especially useful for fire, water and large commercial losses where the scene changes quickly. Our guide to fire damage commercial insurance claims explains why early documentation matters so much in those cases.

Tip: Scan before mitigation crews remove drywall or contents whenever it is safe to do so. Once the scene is cleaned up, the original extent of the damage is hard to prove.

Matterport for Texas storm, water and fire claims

Texas properties see a wide mix of losses: hail and wind across North and Central Texas, hurricane wind and water damage along the Gulf Coast, winter freeze pipe bursts and wildfire in rural areas. Each of those losses changes quickly. Wet drywall gets cut out, smoke-damaged contents get hauled away and temporary repairs cover the original damage.

A Matterport scan made in the first days after the loss freezes the scene. Months later, if there is a disagreement over how many rooms were affected or how high water wicked up the walls, the model answers the question. On large losses, such as apartment complexes, churches or commercial buildings, scanning every unit or area gives the claim a consistent baseline that is hard to dispute. Learn more in our guide to large loss insurance appraisal in Texas.

Matterport in the appraisal process

In an insurance appraisal, both appraisers and the umpire need to agree on the amount of loss. A shared 3D model gives everyone the same view of the property, which narrows arguments about room sizes, the extent of damage and what was there before the loss. It is one of the most useful pieces of evidence during insurance appraisal.

How accurate are Matterport measurements?

Accuracy depends on the capture device, scan spacing and conditions. Matterport publishes accuracy specifications for its cameras, and professional-grade scans are generally accurate enough for room dimensions, quantity checks and floor plans. Smartphone captures are less precise.

For insurance purposes, Matterport measurements are excellent for verifying square footage of walls, floors and ceilings and catching quantity errors in an estimate. For engineering or structural work that requires tight tolerances, critical dimensions should still be verified on site.

Can you use Matterport outdoors?

Yes, with limits. Pro-series cameras with lidar can capture exterior areas like patios, porches and building facades. Bright direct sunlight can interfere with some depth sensors, and large open areas need more scan positions. Roofs are usually better documented with drones or measurement reports. Compare those tools in EagleView vs Matterport for insurance claims and can drones be used for insurance roof inspections.

Matterport cost, downloads and CAD conversion

Is Matterport free to use?

Matterport offers subscription plans at different levels, and has offered a limited free tier for small users. Plans, limits and add-on pricing change over time, so check Matterport's current plans before buying. Hiring a professional to scan a property is another option, and is common for one-time documentation like an insurance claim.

Can you download a Matterport tour?

Viewing a tour happens online, but data files can be exported through paid add-ons. Common exports include point cloud files, 3D mesh files and floor plan images, which can be imported into other software.

Can you convert Matterport to CAD or BIM?

Yes. Point cloud and mesh exports can be brought into CAD and BIM programs, and Matterport offers add-on services that produce CAD floor plans and BIM files from a scan. Architects and contractors use these to plan repairs or renovations from accurate existing conditions.

How long does it take to get a Matterport model?

Capture time depends on the size and complexity of the space. A typical home can often be scanned in one to three hours, while large commercial buildings may take a full day or more. After upload, cloud processing usually finishes within hours to about a day, and then the model is ready to share by link. For insurance documentation, that turnaround means a damaged property can be recorded and shared with adjusters and appraisers within days of the loss, often before mitigation or repairs change the scene.

Who owns Matterport?

Matterport was founded in 2011 and later became a public company. In 2025 it was acquired by CoStar Group, the commercial real estate information company.

The best claim files use all three. Matterport provides the overall record, close-up photos capture fine detail such as hail bruising or water lines, and video can show things like active leaks. Our claim documentation checklist lists what to capture for each type of loss.

Next steps: putting Matterport to work for your property

If you are selling, renovating or managing a building, a Matterport scan creates a lasting digital record you can share with anyone. If you are dealing with property damage, the case is even stronger: a scan made early preserves evidence that cannot be recreated once repairs start.

faqs.q: How long does a Matterport scan take?
faqs.a: A typical single-family home can usually be scanned in one to three hours, depending on size, layout and the level of detail needed. Large commercial buildings take longer. After capture, cloud processing generally takes several hours to a day before the finished 3D tour is ready to share.

faqs.q: Can insurance adjusters use a Matterport tour?
faqs.a: Yes. A Matterport tour is shared by web link, so adjusters, appraisers, umpires and engineers can review a property remotely without special software. They can move through rooms, view the dollhouse model and take measurements, which helps everyone work from the same record of the damage.

faqs.q: Does a Matterport scan replace photos?
faqs.a: Not entirely. A scan captures the whole space in context and allows measurements, but close-up photos still show fine details like hail bruising, water lines and burn patterns more clearly. The strongest claim documentation pairs a Matterport model with targeted close-up photos and notes.

Yes. Measurements can be taken inside the model, and floor plan add-ons can provide room dimensions and area calculations. For insurance purposes this is useful for checking wall, floor and ceiling quantities in an estimate. Critical dimensions for engineering work should still be verified on site.

faqs.q: Is Matterport worth it for a small insurance claim?
faqs.a: For a minor loss with obvious damage, good photos may be enough. Matterport adds the most value on larger, disputed or complex claims, such as fire, water, multi-room or commercial losses, where documenting the full scope and room measurements before repairs begin can make a real difference.
